questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Neel has cleaned his room yesterday.
Neel have cleaned his room yesterday.
questions.rule: Yesterday is a finished past time, so use the simple past cleaned, not the present perfect.

questions.prompt: Which sentence is in the correct passive form?
questions.rule: Present perfect passive: has/have been + past participle. Garden is singular: has been watered.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: The present perfect uses has + past participle: has Neel written. Wrote is the simple past.

Dishes cannot put themselves, so use the passive. Dishes is plural: have been put.
Already goes with the present perfect. With I, use have made.
Unless means 'if ... not'. The unless-clause uses the simple present: unless you make your bed.

options: Yes, Mom. I have watered them.
Yes, Mom. I have water them.
Yes, Mom. I has watered them.
questions.rule: Answer a present perfect question with I have + past participle: I have watered.

chat: Hurry up! The bus leaves at eight.
options: I will miss it unless I will leave now.
I will miss it unless I leave now.
I will missed it unless I leave now.
questions.rule: Main clause: will + base verb. The unless-clause uses the simple present: unless I leave.

questions.source: Neel put the dishes in the dishwasher.
options: The dishes was put in the dishwasher by Neel.
The dishes were put in the dishwasher by Neel.
The dishes were putted in the dishwasher by Neel.
questions.rule: Simple past passive: were (plural dishes) + past participle put (put - put - put).

options: Neel's mother told him cleaning his room.
Neel's mother said him to clean his room.
Neel's mother told him to clean his room.
questions.rule: A reported command is told + person + to + verb. We say told him, not said him.

options: Neel has lived in Pune since five years.
Neel has lived in Pune for five years.
Neel is living in Pune since five years.
questions.rule: Use for with a length of time (five years) and since with a starting point (2020).

questions.before: You can't play Chaupar unless you
questions.rule: After unless, use the simple present for a present or future idea: unless you finish.
A reported yes/no question uses whether + statement order, and the tense moves back: he had cleaned.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to make a passive sentence.
questions.rule: Simple past passive: were + past participle taken.

chat: Shall we play cricket after lunch?
questions.rule: After unless, use the simple present, and it takes -s: unless it rains.

questions.source: Mom said to Neel, "Make your bed."
options: Mom told Neel to make your bed.
Mom told Neel to make his bed.
Mom told Neel that make his bed.
questions.rule: A command becomes told + person + to + verb, and your changes to his.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Present perfect: have washed. Both my friends is plural: are waiting.

options: The groceries have been bring home.
The groceries has been brought home.
The groceries have been brought home.
questions.rule: Groceries is plural: have been + past participle brought.

options: Unless you hurry, you will miss the puppet show.
Unless you don't hurry, you will miss the puppet show.
Unless you will hurry, you will miss the puppet show.
questions.rule: Unless already means 'if not', so never add don't; and use the simple present after it.

questions.rule: Class 1 is a starting point, so use since. For goes with a length of time (for five years).
One past action happened before another (the rains came), so use the past perfect passive: had been patched.

questions.rule: A reported question uses statement order and moves the tense back: why he had to make his bed.
In a reported question the verb comes after the subject: what grinding stones were.

chat: Have you ever seen a grinding stone?
options: Yes, I have seen one at Nani's house last year.
Yes, I saw one at Nani's house last year.
Yes, I have saw one at Nani's house last year.
questions.rule: Last year is a finished time, so the reply needs the simple past: I saw one.

chat: Will you come to the puppet show tonight?
options: I will come if Aai will let me.
I will come if Aai lets me.
I came if Aai lets me.
questions.rule: First conditional: if + simple present, main clause will + verb: I will come if Aai lets me.

questions.source: If you do not try, you cannot build a robot.
options: Unless you do not try, you cannot build a robot.
Unless you try, you cannot build a robot.
Unless you try, you can build a robot.
questions.rule: If ... not becomes unless; drop the not from that clause only. The main clause stays the same.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Reported past fact: you had many chores. After did, use the base verb: did you carry.

options: Your bed must be made before you go out.
Your bed must made before you go out.
Your bed must be make before you go out.
questions.rule: Modal passive: modal + be + past participle: must be made.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Told takes a person directly (told Matadevi). Said needs to before the person.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Passive: were + past participle: bricks that were carved by hand.

questions.before: If I had a robot, it
questions.rule: Second conditional (imaginary): if + past, then would + base verb: it would make.
Present perfect question: Have + subject + ever + past participle.

chat: What did your mom say when you came home late?
options: She asked me where had I been all evening.
She asked me where I had been all evening.
She asked me where I have been all evening.
questions.rule: Reported question: statement order (I had been) and the tense moves back after asked.

chat: Who painted the backdrop for our skit?
options: It was painted by Riya and I.
It was paint by Riya and me.
It was painted by Riya and me.
questions.rule: Passive: was painted. After by, use the object pronoun: by Riya and me.

options: The garden have been watered by me.
The garden has been watered by me.
The garden had been watered by me.
questions.rule: Present perfect passive: has been + past participle. Keep the same tense as the active.

questions.source: The 1910 boy said, "I promised to go to the riverside with my friends."
options: The 1910 boy said that he had promised to go to the riverside with his friends.
The 1910 boy said that I had promised to go to the riverside with my friends.
The 1910 boy said that he has promised to go to the riverside with his friends.
questions.rule: I ... my become he ... his, and the simple past promised moves back to had promised.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 3 errors in this diary entry.
questions.rule: Every boy ... was; passive was fetched; after will, the base verb complain.

options: If Neel would have made his bed earlier, he would have reached the park on time.
If Neel had made his bed earlier, he would reached the park on time.
If Neel had made his bed earlier, he would have reached the park on time.
questions.rule: Third conditional: if + had + past participle, then would have + past participle.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Present perfect passive: has been + past participle: has been finished.

questions.after: ever make his bed for him.
questions.rule: Reported questions use statement order: whether a robot would ever make... - no question order inside.

questions.prompt: Put the words in order to make a passive sentence.
questions.rule: Past perfect passive: had been + past participle: had been cleared.

chat: You were late for the match. What happened?
options: If I left on time, I wouldn't have missed the bus.
If I had left on time, I wouldn't have missed the bus.
If I had left on time, I won't have missed the bus.
questions.rule: For a past regret, use the third conditional: if I had left ..., I wouldn't have missed.

questions.source: The 1800 boy said, "Mother, why do I have to make the beds?"
options: The 1800 boy asked his mother why he had to make the beds.
The 1800 boy asked his mother why did he have to make the beds.
The 1800 boy asked his mother why he has to make the beds.
questions.rule: A wh-question becomes asked + wh-word + statement order, with the tense moved back: why he had to.

options: By whom was the grinding stones cleaned?
By whom were the grinding stones cleaned?
By whom were the grinding stones clean?
questions.rule: Who becomes By whom; plural stones take were + past participle cleaned.

questions.source: You will not get a robot if you do not work hard.
options: You will not get a robot unless you do not work hard.
You will not get a robot unless you work hard.
You will get a robot unless you work hard.
questions.rule: If ... not becomes unless + positive verb. The main clause keeps its not.
